newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sabena returns to fitness.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sabena returns to fitness.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena SA said on Friday that earnings in the first four months of 1997 showed it was on track for a return to profit from 1998.

"We're certainly on budget for the first four months, and based on provisional bookings, the first half is looking good while we can also be positive for the full year," Sabena spokesman Erik Sclep said.
Sclep said that January had still been well below expectations but that the situation had improved thereafter and that April had exceeded every forecast.
"We can't really say we're already there but we're certainly on the right track," he said.
The number of passengers transported in the first four months of 1997 was roughly equal to that for the first six months of 1996, he said.
SAirGroup, the holding group which includes Swissair, will assess its cooperation with Sabena at the end of June and had warned the Belgian carrier it had to be in line with budget.
SAirGroup expects Sabena to reach break even in 1998 "and we think we can make it", Sclep said.

SAirGroup decided to fully write down the value of its 49.5 percent Sabena stake, acquired in 1995, in 1996 accounts, after Sabena made a 1996 consolidated loss after provisions of 8.87 billion francs ($252.7 million).
